messages:
alex (Sales): Heads up — procurement at RedwoodHealth flagged two blockers on the PO/orderform for the POC: 1) they insist on e-sign with identity verification (DocuSign ID check or notarized bank letter) for countersigners, and 2) they want a 99.9% SLA with service credits. Can legal and eng weigh in?

maria (Legal): Thanks — do we have the customer's exact redline requests? If they sent text, paste it here. Also need to know whether this is for a hosted consumption agreement or reserved/dedicated capacity (affects SLA/penalty language).

alex (Sales): Copied the excerpt they pasted into the procurement ticket: "Customer requires e-sign identity verification for all signers and reserves the right to require notarized signature for contract values >$250k. The Provider shall provide an SLA of 99.9% uptime, with service credits scaling to 10% of monthly fees for each 0.1% below the target, capped at 50%." This is a POC — estimated commit $45k for 3 months if we do a dedicated mini-pool.

cheng (Solutions): For the POC we're proposing a small dedicated pool (single-tenant) to match their data isolation ask. Engineering: can we meet DocuSign identity flows and the SLA expectation for a dedicated pool?

eli (Engineering): We can integrate with DocuSign for envelope signing; DocuSign ID verification is external to our infra (we just accept signed artifacts). On SLA: 99.9% for a small dedicated pool is aggressive for a short POC timeframe — our platform targeting for Dedicated is usually 99.5% with the Dedicated contractual package. For hosted customers we have historical 99.9+ availability across regions, but not guaranteed for tiny isolated test pools.

maria (Legal): That aligns with precedent. For short-term POCs we typically counter to 99.5% and a limited credit cap (e.g., credits capped at monthly POC fees, not a percentage cliff). Proposed reply language: "For Proof-of-Concept engagements, Provider offers a 99.5% uptime SLA. Service credit remedies for POCs shall not exceed the total fees paid for the POC term." Is that acceptable to Sales/Finance?

alex (Sales): Procurement will push back on the 99.5. Can we offer an escrowed remediation or a one-time goodwill credit bumped to 7.5% if they sign an annual Dedicated commit after POC? Might be a negotiation point.

taylor (Finance): We can offer a conditional bump to 7.5% one-time credit tied to an annual commit conversion clause. Prefer caps expressed as absolute dollar amounts (easier for accounting). Example: "Credits limited to $X for the POC; if Customer converts to annual commit within 60 days, Provider will issue a one-time additional credit equal to Y% of the POC fees, not to exceed $Z." Finance will need the POC fee number to set $X/$Z.

maria (Legal): Good. I'll draft a short redline for the OF/MSA: (1) swap SLA to 99.5% for POC, cap credits to POC fees, include auto-convert credit language; (2) add clause: "Provider accepts electronic signatures via DocuSign; identity verification performed by DocuSign satisfies Provider's signing policy. Provider is not responsible for third-party ID verification failures." That should address the ID verification ask without agreeing to notarization. Any objections?

cheng (Solutions): No objections. From product side, confirm that the dedicated pool config we quoted can be spun up under 5 business days — we should call that out in the OF. Also add a line item for "Reserved POC capacity — refundable credit upon conversion" so procurement sees the accounting path.

alex (Sales): Procurement also asked for the PO number flow: they want the PO returned on the invoice and the countersign path to include their procurement approver + legal. I'll route a DocuSign envelope to their two signers and our AE + legal countersigner. Maria — can you be the countersigner or delegate?

maria (Legal): I can countersign. I'll prepare the redline and send back in the ticket by EOD. If they insist on notarization for >$250k, call it out as a special escalation and we'll require paper or a signed notary addendum — but at $45k POC we're not accepting notarized requirement.

docsign-bot: DocuSign envelope template "Redwood POC OF" created — use template id tpl_2781. Reminder: set authentication to "ID Check" for customer signers if requested.

eli (Engineering): One more note — if we promise dedicated pool SLA we should include a clause about scheduled maintenance windows and what counts as downtime (control plane vs inference plane). I'll drop suggested language into the ticket to avoid ambiguity.

alex (Sales): Perfect. Plan: Maria will upload redline, Eli will add technical SLA carveouts, Finance will provide dollar caps once we lock POC fee, and I'll draft the DocuSign envelope routing. Thanks all — please flag if procurement pushes notarization again. :thumbsup:
